brief_item.title: 分形KV缓存档案实现无损压缩与原地检索
brief_item.direction_name: 压缩、增量传输、预取与放置
brief_item.core_conclusion: 分形档案格式用收缩迭代映射码序列化符号，支持O(1)随机访问、摊余追加与近似子串检索。
brief_item.mechanism: 收缩迭代映射码将符号序列序列化为低维实向量，形成无损归档与索引。
brief_item.result: 36倍压缩下困惑度仅增11.2%，编码0.68微秒/字符，检索311微秒。
brief_item.boundary: 仅在124M参数模型验证，缺乏下游任务评估与生产部署数据。
brief_item.project_relevance: 高压缩比与O(1)访问支持跨域缓存选择性传输，K/V非对称量化指导带宽质量权衡。

facts.title: Fractal KV-Cache Archives: Lossless Symbolic Storage with In-Place Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Inference
facts.event_hint: arXiv research paper on fractal-based KV cache compression archive format
facts.problem: KV cache dominates memory cost of long-context autoregressive inference; existing compression (quantization, eviction, offloading) addresses the lossy compression step, but the question of how to store the resulting symbol stream and whether the storage layer can enable retrieval and random access remains unaddressed.
facts.mechanism: Contractive iterated-map codes (chaos game representation/universal sequence maps) serialize symbol sequences into low-dimensional real vectors, forming a lossless archive with O(1) random access, O(1) amortized append, linear-time encoding, and in-place substring search capability on stored vectors.

evidence.claim: Per-head residual VQ with hybrid bit allocation (K×4, V×2) achieves 36× compression vs fp16 at +11.2% perplexity cost
evidence.condition: GPT-2 124M, 1024-token context, 4-sink + 32-recent exact window, The Time Machine corpus

evidence.claim: Quantizing keys is ~4× more damaging to perplexity than quantizing values
evidence.baseline: values-only quantization (+4.0% perplexity) vs keys-only quantization (+14.5% perplexity)
evidence.condition: GPT-2, 1024-token context, per-head RVQ k=256×2 base configuration
evidence.source_locator: Table 2 and surrounding text, PDF Page 4

evidence.claim: Encoding performance: 0.68µs/char, 311µs random access lookup, 175µs/token append
Per-head codebooks Pareto-dominate pooled codebooks at equal bit budget
Archive supports approximate substring queries directly on stored vectors with full recall
evidence.baseline: sequential decoding required for arithmetic coding
evidence.condition: Stored vectors enable nearest-neighbor distance as graded suffix-similarity

facts.evaluation_context: GPT-2 (124M parameters), The Time Machine corpus (public domain), 1024-token contexts, single laptop CPU, exact window = 4 attention sinks + 32 recent tokens (3.5% of context at 1024), perplexity as sole quality metric, exact baseline perplexity = 35.97, codebooks trained on disjoint span of same book via k-means
facts.limitations: Small-scale study on single 124M-parameter model; only perplexity measured (no downstream task accuracy); per-head codebooks trained per-corpus not amortized; retrieval limited to suffix matching not semantic retrieval; serialization advantage is access pattern not compression ratio (uniform code 6.13 bits/char vs ~2.55 bits/char for order-2 model); larger models may tolerate more KV quantization but unvalidated
facts.project_relevance: Relevant to cross-domain cache transfer as the fractal archive format provides: (1) high compression (36×) enabling lower bandwidth transfer of archived KV states; (2) O(1) random access enabling selective retrieval rather than full-cache transfer; (3) in-place search index for matching cached contexts; (4) linear-time encoding/decoding suitable for streaming transfers. The bit-asymmetric K/V quantization insight informs bandwidth-quality tradeoffs for cross-domain cache replication.
source_notes: arXiv v2 published 2026-08-05 (dated August 7, 2026 in paper)
All experiments reproducible from single command on laptop CPU

brief_item.title: 稀疏张量核心与三层存储格式加速GPU稀疏推理
brief_item.direction_name: 芯片内存接口、数据搬移与软硬件协同
brief_item.core_conclusion: 三层矩阵存储格式联合稀疏张量核心与CUDA核心，实现50%稀疏度GPU推理加速。
brief_item.mechanism: Sparse-TC层利用稀疏张量核心，Slot-Filling层用PDD编码压缩，残差层存储非零元。
brief_item.result: H100上50%稀疏度时解码内核1.64倍于SpInfer，峰值内存降21.4%。
brief_item.boundary: 缺乏绝对吞吐量、HBM带宽利用率与功耗能效数据，仅限解码阶段。
brief_item.project_relevance: 展示算法硬件协同设计缓解GPU内存带宽瓶颈，但缺关键部署指标验证。

facts.title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices
facts.event_hint: DAC 2026 paper proposing sparse matrix inference acceleration for LLMs on GPUs
facts.problem: At moderate unstructured sparsity (~50%), existing GPU kernels for sparse matrix multiplication (SpMM) cannot outperform dense counterparts, limiting inference acceleration while maintaining model quality.
facts.mechanism: Three-layer matrix storage format: (i) Sparse-TC layer enabling sparse tensor cores to accelerate SpMM; (ii) Slot-Filling layer using parallel differential distance (PDD) encoding for matrix compression with low-cost on-chip decoding; (iii) lightweight Residual Layer (CSR format) for remaining non-zeros. Co-optimized SpMM kernel jointly utilizes sparse tensor cores and CUDA cores with pipelined execution overlapping computation with memory access.

evidence.claim: Kernel achieves up to 1.64× speedup over SpInfer at 50% sparsity
Kernel achieves up to 1.81× speedup over FlashLLM at 50% sparsity
End-to-end inference throughput up to 41.4% higher than FlashLLM for OPT-30B
Peak memory usage reduced by 21.4% compared to dense baseline
Format conversion cost is one-time: 41.1s for OPT-30B, 92.6s for OPT-66B

facts.evaluation_context: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPUs with 80GB HBM3, NVLink interconnect; OPT-30B and OPT-66B models pruned with Wanda algorithm; batch sizes 8/16/32; sparsity levels 50%/60%/70%; input/output sequence length 512; GCC 12.3.0 and NVCC 12.6.
facts.limitations: Does not outperform FlashLLM under high sparsity due to zero-padding requirements; constrained during compute-bound prefill phase with large N (runs slower than cuBLAS); targets decoding phase optimization; requires GPUs with sparse tensor cores and HBM; incurs slightly higher memory usage than SpInfer due to bitmap encoding in baseline method. Absolute throughput in tokens/second or latency in milliseconds not reported. HBM bandwidth utilization or memory traffic measurements not provided. Power consumption or performance-per-watt not measured. Supplement contains only acknowledgments and references—no additional experimental data addressing evidence gaps.
facts.project_relevance: Addresses GPU memory bandwidth bottleneck in LLM inference through sparse matrix computation co-design with modern GPU hardware (sparse tensor cores + HBM). Relevant to direction on AI accelerator memory interface and hardware-software co-design. Demonstrates 1.64× kernel speedup and 21.4% memory reduction at 50% sparsity on H100, showing how algorithm-hardware specialization can extract performance from memory-bound workloads. However, absolute throughput numbers (tokens/second), HBM bandwidth utilization measurements, and power efficiency metrics are not reported—key evidence gaps for assessing real-world deployment value.

evidence_gaps.question: What is the absolute throughput in tokens/second or latency in milliseconds for OPT-30B and OPT-66B at batch sizes 8/16/32?
What are the specific HBM bandwidth utilization numbers or memory traffic measurements?
What is the power consumption or performance-per-watt compared to dense baselines?

brief_item.title: GPUSparse：GPU加速稀疏检索实现235倍加速
brief_item.direction_name: 芯片内存接口、数据搬移与软硬件协同
brief_item.core_conclusion: GPUSparse通过GPU并行倒排索引和批量scatter-add评分算法，在880万文档上实现235倍加速，达到787 QPS吞吐。
brief_item.mechanism: 采用块对齐warp合并posting列表和批量scatter-add内核，单次处理数百查询。
brief_item.result: 相比Pyserini CPU实现加速235倍至9.6ms，文档并行内核达62.6%峰值HBM带宽。
brief_item.boundary: 单查询9.6ms高于CPU近似搜索，批次500需44GB显存。
brief_item.project_relevance: 展示H100上带宽受限稀疏检索模式，权衡是根本设计选择。

facts.title: GPUSparse: GPU-Accelerated Learned Sparse Retrieval with Parallel Inverted Indices
facts.event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-06-24 on GPU-accelerated exact learned sparse retrieval using parallel inverted indices
facts.problem: Learned sparse retrieval models (SPLADE) achieve quality competitive with dense models while preserving interpretability, but inference-time scoring relies on CPU-bound inverted index traversal algorithms (WAND, Block-Max WAND). This creates a fundamental bottleneck for real-time serving at scale. Existing GPU sparse retrieval systems (Seismic) trade 25% recall for speed.
facts.mechanism: GPUSparse introduces: (1) GPU-parallel inverted index with block-aligned, warp-coalesced posting lists, (2) batched scatter-add scoring algorithm processing hundreds of queries simultaneously, (3) fused Triton kernels. The scatter-add kernel processes only O(q_bar * L_bar) entries per query (query terms × posting lists). A document-parallel kernel trades work-efficiency for bandwidth utilization.

evidence.claim: 235x speedup over Pyserini CPU exact scoring at 8.8M documents
evidence.condition: MS MARCO passage ranking 8.8M passages, batch 500, H100 80GB

evidence.claim: Achieves 787 QPS throughput at 8.8M documents with batch 500
evidence.condition: MS MARCO 8.8M passages, batch 500, H100 80GB, exact scoring

evidence.claim: Document-parallel kernel achieves 62.6% of H100 peak HBM bandwidth
Scatter-add kernel achieves 12.5 GB/s effective bandwidth (0.37% of peak) due to scattered atomic writes
8.5 GB for inverted index at 8.8M passages (11% of 80GB H100)

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated on MS MARCO passage ranking (8.8M passages) with real SPLADE embeddings. Hardware: H100 80GB GPU. Metrics include MRR@10, Recall@1000, per-query latency, QPS throughput. Cross-domain validation on BEIR benchmarks (SciFact, NFCorpus, TREC-COVID). Comparison against Pyserini CPU exact scoring, Seismic (fastest CPU sparse), cuSPARSE SpMV, and dense matmul ground truth.
facts.limitations: GPU cost: H100 GPU is substantially more expensive than CPU-only retrieval. Single-query latency 9.6ms at 8.8M docs - CPU methods faster for single-query approximate search. Score buffer memory scales as O(B*N): 44GB at batch 500 with 8.8M docs (55% of H100). No dynamic updates without full index rebuild. 6x slower than Seismic for approximate top-10 retrieval at 8.8M.
facts.project_relevance: GPUSparse demonstrates memory-bandwidth-bound sparse retrieval on H100 with 62.6% peak utilization achieved via document-parallel kernel. The work-efficiency vs bandwidth-efficiency tradeoff is fundamental: scatter-add processes only query-relevant postings (work-efficient) at 0.37% bandwidth utilization, while doc-parallel achieves 62.6% peak but reads 76GB vs 0.09GB per batch. The 8.5GB index size at 8.8M passages shows sparse format memory advantage vs dense (~1TB). Index cannot be updated without full rebuild - limitation for dynamic workloads.

facts.title: Looping Is Not Reliability: State-Bound Evidence and Typed Revision Contracts for Agentic Code Repair
facts.event_hint: AgenticDev 2026 study on correctness regression in agentic code repair loops
facts.problem: Generate-test-revise loops in coding agents provide no reliability guarantee; correct patches can be destroyed in subsequent revisions, stale observations can revive old bugs, and correlated verifiers can confirm the same error
facts.mechanism: State-bound typed revision contract that binds verifier evidence to exact code states, preserves verified checkpoints, and emits auditable admission receipts; separates admission, preservation, grounded certification, competence, and liveness

evidence.claim: Current correctness falls from 0.820 after one revision to 0.673 after two revisions
evidence.condition: Forced revision protocol, current traces, 30 HumanEval repairs, 900 three-revision trajectories
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5, Results section, Figure 1b discussion

evidence.claim: Ever-correct rate rises to 0.847 despite current correctness decline
evidence.condition: Cumulative discovery metric, 30 HumanEval repairs, three-revision trajectories
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5, Results section, Figure 1b discussion

evidence.claim: Stale traces harm 34/135 correct starts versus 4/135 with current traces, a 22.2-point increase
evidence.condition: 14B model replication, prespecified study, task-cluster 95% CI [8.9, 37.0], exact Holm p=0.0337
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5, Results section, RQ2 discussion

evidence.claim: 16.0% of trajectories produce correct patch then lose it by revision 3
Reference implementation is executable specification, not evidence of improved repair competence
evidence.condition: Post-study implementation; not used to generate empirical results

facts.evaluation_context: Sealed five-seed study over 30 HumanEval repairs producing 900 three-revision trajectories. Two common-state studies use 2,430 branches from identical frozen programs to remove post-treatment risk-set bias. Prespecified 14B replication with 135 starts per condition. Repository experiments over 24 bugs and four coder stacks (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct-AWQ, Qwen3-Coder-Next-FP8, Devstral Small 2 24B). Reference implementation developed after empirical study completed.
facts.limitations: Study scoped to HumanEval repair under forced-revision protocol; does not show adaptive loops must regress but demonstrates need for preservation and stopping rules. Repository experiments exposed floor effects and component heterogeneity without Holm-significant effects. Reference implementation is executable specification for contract enforcement, not evidence of improved repair competence or calibrated verifier dependence.
facts.project_relevance: Relevant to agent acceleration project questions on whether parallel tool calls or caching introduce correctness risk. Demonstrates that stale feedback harms correct starts (22.2-point increase in harm). State-bound evidence binding suggests approach for ensuring tool-call reuse and read results are tied to exact code states. However, limited to code repair domain; direct applicability to read/grep acceleration unclear.
